about: The face set: free faces whose licence allows commercial use in video (SIL Open Font License 1.1, checked in each package's LICENSE and metadata), grouped by look, each with its display and text pairing, weights, optical size and the setting that reads premium. scripts/add-font.mjs fetches one from @fontsource-variable (npm pack into a temp folder, nothing installed) into the film's src/brand/fonts/; deck.py deals a face from the dealt type option's look; font-match.mjs ranks these first. TYPE's house numbers (src/brand/tokens.ts, lib/look.ts TYPE_LOOK) are written for the default face, Inter, at its display cut. Every other face carries weight_offset (add it to every TYPE weight so the stems match Inter's) and offset_em (add it to every TYPE tracking so a line sets to Inter's width at the same x-height): both measured with node scripts/font-match.mjs --like <Inter opsz file> --like-weight 500 --text "ask three models at once". The starter also BUNDLES the faces of the type pairings (assets/remotion-starter/public/fonts, licences in its fonts.json): `pairs` lists them; scripts/type-deal.ts deals one per film from the product's name (src/fx/TypePairs.ts holds the weights, optical tracking and leads) and writes FONT.text (the voice), FONT.ui (the text face) and the TYPE roles; no fetch, no add-font step.

looks.name: neutral premium grotesk
looks.for: the default for launch, product and feature films and walkthroughs: the quiet, exact grotesk of premium product type. Personality comes from size, weight, tracking and motion, not from the letterforms.

looks.name: tight display grotesk
looks.for: big, firm headline systems set tight, flush left or cropped by the frame: ads, teasers and reels cut on the beat (the bold type family). One family for every role: Inter Tight holds UI and caption sizes at film scale; the bold family's numbers plus its +0.03 em offset set it.

looks.name: soft geometric product sans
looks.for: round, open, friendly-precise product type: consumer apps, assistants, platforms, a marketplace. Urbanist when the brand wants the single-storey a; Google Sans Flex when one family must also give a softer (ROND) or wider (wdth) cut.

looks.name: friendly open grotesk
looks.for: calm, warm, approachable brands (care, learning, community, consumer ads in a feed). Manrope runs light: its stems match Inter's 100 units heavier, so its weights sit a step above the house numbers.

looks.name: technical grotesk with its mono
looks.for: developer tools, APIs, infrastructure, data: a grotesk with a real mono for code, logs, figures and tags. JetBrains Mono when code is on screen for long.

inter.notes: the default. Load opsz.css (weight and optical size): at 32 px and up the browser sets the display cut by itself (font-optical-sizing: auto), which is every size a film holds; the plain index.css is the text cut only and sets loose and wide at film sizes. Cap height 0.727 em, x-height 0.55 em.

inter-tight.notes: Inter's display cut spaced tight for headlines, the whole film's family in the tight look. It sets 6 % narrower than Inter at the same x-height, so every TYPE tracking takes +0.03 em.

geist.notes: a crisper, more technical grotesk; sets 2 % wider than Inter. The technical look, with Geist Mono.

dm-sans.notes: low-contrast geometric with round bowls and open apertures; load opsz.css so 40 px and up take the display cut. Sets to Inter's width at the same tracking.

google-sans-flex.notes: a geometric product sans with an optical size that reaches 144, so hero and giant words get a true display cut; full.css adds width (wdth) and roundness (ROND, a softer friendly cut). Sets 6 % narrower than Inter at the same x-height: every TYPE tracking takes +0.03 em. The latin opsz file is 117 KB; full.css (every axis) is 1.4 MB.

urbanist.notes: geometric with a single-storey a and round, open letters; runs light (stems match Inter's 90 units heavier).

manrope.notes: a warm, open grotesk with a semi-geometric skeleton; runs light (stems match Inter's 110 units heavier): set text at 500 and display at 600-700.

plus-jakarta-sans.notes: friendly, slightly wide geometric-grotesk with a large x-height; runs light.

public-sans.notes: a sturdy neutral grotesk that holds a heavy wordmark or a firm headline well; sets 4 % wider than Inter.

geist-mono.notes: the default mono: code, terminal output, aligned figures, small caps tags (+0.04 to +0.08 em).

jetbrains-mono.notes: a mono built for reading code on screen for long: an editor or a terminal held for seconds.

instrument-sans.set_by: its pairing in src/fx/TypePairs.ts (weights and optical tracking per role)
instrument-sans.notes: crisp Swiss editorial grotesk, a little narrow; the swiss pairing voice

schibsted-grotesk.set_by: its pairing in src/fx/TypePairs.ts (weights and optical tracking per role)
schibsted-grotesk.notes: a sturdy newsroom grotesk; its tabular set spaces punctuation like figures (numeralStyle sets proportional)

host-grotesk.set_by: its pairing in src/fx/TypePairs.ts (weights and optical tracking per role)
host-grotesk.notes: contemporary studio grotesk with soft terminals

funnel-display.set_by: its pairing in src/fx/TypePairs.ts (weights and optical tracking per role)
funnel-display.notes: a display grotesk with cut details; pairs with Funnel Sans

funnel-sans.set_by: its pairing in src/fx/TypePairs.ts (weights and optical tracking per role)

mona-sans.set_by: its pairing in src/fx/TypePairs.ts (weights and optical tracking per role)
mona-sans.notes: registered twice: Mona Sans (wdth 75-125) and Mona Sans Wide (fixed 112.5 %), the wide pairing voice

hanken-grotesk.set_by: its pairing in src/fx/TypePairs.ts (weights and optical tracking per role)
hanken-grotesk.notes: a neat neo-grotesk, light on its feet

bricolage-grotesque.set_by: its pairing in src/fx/TypePairs.ts (weights and optical tracking per role)
bricolage-grotesque.notes: ink traps and character at display sizes (optical sizes); the expressive pairing voice

setting: One PAIRING per film (scripts/type-deal.ts deals it, src/fx/TypePairs.ts sets it): the voice for every statement, the claim and the wordmark (FONT.text), the text face for product UI and captions (FONT.ui), two or three weights each, plus the mono only for code, logs and aligned data. Never the same voice two films in a row.
Statements regular to medium (Inter 450-500, the bold family 600); 650 and up only for a wordmark or one claim on the accent. A sentence at 700 reads heavy and generated.

Tracking: the calm family keeps the face's own fit (in Inter: UI and captions +0.01 em, the line 0, display and hero -0.01, a whole giant word +0.02); the bold family tightens as size grows (-0.03 for the line to -0.045 for the giant); small capitals labels +0.04 to +0.08. Another face adds its offset_em to every role.

Optical size: load the opsz file of a face that has one (Inter, DM Sans, Google Sans Flex) and leave font-optical-sizing on auto, so display sizes take the display cut; measure with the same settings (lib/measure.ts measures the DOM, so it does).
Sentence case for every line; capitals only for labels of one or two words.

Figures: tabular for anything that counts, changes or aligns (typeStyle sets them); a single static hero number may take proportional figures (fontVariantNumeric: 'proportional-nums') so a 1 does not leave a gap.
Lead 1.05 for display, 1.2 for a sentence line, 1.3 for UI and captions.
No rounded, techno, script, condensed or serif face as the film's voice; a face outside the set is checked with font-match against the set first and recorded with its reason in TREATMENT.md.
